extrait: Includes the return of Now & Later Packs, MLB The Show 26 community stats, and more. Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back. As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been playing for decades or joined us for the first time this year, you’ve helped make this another special chapter in our franchise’s history. While we’re proud of what our team accomplished this year, we recognize that the heart of MLB The Show has always been its community. Since launch, you’ve hit an astonishing: You’ve also drawn 123,300,616 walks and racked up a staggering 2,130,551,161 strikeouts. It seems we have some work to do on our collective plate discipline and pitch recognition! But it’s not all strikeouts. You’ve also recorded 18,666,758 Perfect-Perfect hits and scored an incredible 2,506,757,548 runs. And if those numbers weren’t impressive enough, the community collectively spent the equivalent of 31,541 years playing MLB The Show this year. This year was not without some issues and hopefully over the next few months we’ll show you how we’ve made improvements in a host of areas.Your stories, feedback, creativity, and passion remind us why we do what we do. We don’t take your time, trust, or support for granted, and we’re incredibly fortunate to have a community that cares so deeply about the game. From all of us at San Diego Studio, thank you for another unforgettable year. We’re excited about what lies ahead and look forward to continuing this journey together. So, what lies ahead? We’re eager to share the exciting new features and improvements coming to MLB The Show 27, but it’s still a little too early to reveal what’s in store. However, there’s one announcement we can’t wait to make: The Tech Test is officially returning for MLB The Show 27. Tech Tests are invaluable to the development process. They help our team identify bugs, evaluate performance, and gather meaningful feedback from the community before the game officially launches. Now, you might be wondering: If Tech Tests are so important, why haven’t we held one since MLB The Show 23? That’s a fair question.
